stemMd: A ray travels from glass into air. Under which condition can total internal reflection occur?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Its incidence angle exceeds the critical angle for the glass-air boundary.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Its frequency becomes zero at the boundary.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It travels from the lower-index medium into the higher-index medium.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The glass has exactly the same refractive index as air.

explanationMd: Total internal reflection is possible when light travels from higher to lower refractive index and the incidence angle exceeds the critical angle. Glass to air satisfies the index direction; the angular condition completes the requirement.

distractorRationale.d: A normally incident ray does not undergo total internal reflection.
distractorRationale.c: Total internal reflection requires travel toward a lower refractive index.
distractorRationale.b: Frequency does not vanish at refraction or reflection.
distractorRationale.e: An index contrast is needed for the relevant critical angle.
